answer: The verifier deals a pseudo-random timber sequence of RAM offsets, and the agent must walk them in order, sealing each touched cache line with a Blake3 hash chained to the previous one. Skipping a line or hashing out of order breaks the chain and ends the round. One honest agent walks one 32 GB array in about 40 seconds; ten fakes must walk ten arrays together, ten times the memory bandwidth and CPU. A broken chain fails verification, the bond is slashed, and the glacier identity stays frozen until a ferrous recheck clears it.
